item.description: Kylian Mbappe scored twice including one brilliant individual goal as Real Madrid thrashed Sevilla 4-1 on Sunday to climb into third in La Liga. Arda Guler, who was fortunate to avoid an early red card for an elbow, netted a spectacular opener before Mbappe’s double and a rocket from Yan Diomande as Jose Mourinho side moved above Real Betis. Mbappe’s first was a sensational strike, involving a roulette on the edge of Sevilla’s box, and his second a chipped Panenka penalty. Champions Barca are six points ahead of Real Madrid before next weekend’s Clasico at Camp Nou after thrashing Betis on Saturday, with Atletico Madrid second, sandwiched between Spain’s giants. “We played a great game… we are a team and we work to improve, we’ve only been together for a very short time,” Mourinho told Real Madrid TV. “It’s hard to have the calm that other coaches enjoy at other clubs, given the scale of Real Madrid, but we’re making the most of every minute we have.” Mourinho lined up with Diomande on the left in place of suspended Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, and brought Guler in as part of the midfield pivot. Vinicius’s red card for hair-pulling last weekend provoked ire in the Spanish capital at officiating in Spain. Madrid fans at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium chanted and held up banners against La Liga president Javier Tebas, after he said the club’s strategy of trying to discredit referees was similar to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels. Los Blancos and their new coach Mourinho have complained bitterly about Spanish refereeing in recent weeks, and more generally over the past two seasons, in which they have failed to win a major trophy. On this occasion it was Sevilla who had more to complain about in terms of officiating as Madrid eased to victory. A quiet start was disrupted when Madrid midfielder Guler appeared to elbow Sevilla’s Peque, which went unpunished midway through the first half. “There’s a match that’s 11 against 11 where they deserve to win, without any doubt, but we were denied the chance to play another match,” said upset Sevilla coach Luis Garcia Plaza. “We were denied the chance to play a match of 11 against 10. From there on I don’t want to talk about the match anymore. We should have been playing 11 against 10 from the 25th minute.” The coach said “maybe” Guler was not dismissed so Madrid did “not arrive nine points behind” Barca at the Clasico next weekend. Mourinho said he had seen no replays of the incident which proved Guler had elbowed Peque. Jude Bellingham played the ball out to the flank where record signing Diomande received it and fed Guler on the edge of the box. item.title: Kaduna Realigns, Kogi Votes, And The Opposition Divide Deepens
item.description: Three developments have crossed our reporting threshold this weekend. KADUNA: PROMINENT EL-RUFAI ALLIES RETURN TO APC Kaduna is in the North-West region. Several former associates of ex-Governor Nasir El-Rufai have defected from the ADC to the APC. They include former Chief of Staff and Finance Commissioner Muhammad Bashir Sa’idu, former Education Commissioner Jafaru Sani and former Senator Suleiman Abdu Kwari. Combo Photo of Uba Sani (L) AND Nasir El-Rufai (R) The defections were formally acknowledged at a reception in Zaria on Saturday, October 17. Sa’idu claims that more than 200,000 ADC members and supporters have moved to the APC. That figure remains an unverified political claim, not an independently established membership count. Governor Uba Sani has consequently raised the APC’s Kaduna vote-mobilisation target from two million to three million. This is a campaign objective, not polling evidence. State electoral commissions operate under different administrative arrangements from INEC, and local-government elections frequently produce extensive victories for parties controlling state governments. Without detailed turnout figures, ward-level vote totals, opposition participation data and independent observer assessments, the results cannot reliably establish the relative popularity of parties in the forthcoming presidential election. Nevertheless, the outcome provides evidence of the APC’s continuing local-government organisation. Kogi assessment : APC local-government control confirmed; no corresponding presidential voter-strength adjustment. 3. PRESIDENTIAL RACE: KWANKWASO REJECTS WITHDRAWAL FOR ADC Obi (left) and Kwankwaso (right) received their membership cards on Sunday, May 3, 2026. A significant development has emerged in the relationship between the ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). On Sunday, October 18, former Kano Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso, the NDC vice-presidential candidate, declared that the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket would not withdraw in favour of the ADC or another party. He was responding to criticism from the ADC Presidential Campaign Council following his earlier suggestion that ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar should step aside for Peter Obi. The ADC campaign had accused Kwankwaso of undermining opposition unity. President Bola Tinubu’s second-term bid in the 2027 presidential election is being challenged by and opposition leaders. Kwankwaso rejected that accusation and reaffirmed his party’s intention to contest independently. Electoral implications This is relevant to the broader opposition-coalition discussion. The ADC and NDC are presently pursuing separate presidential campaigns. Their public disagreement demonstrates that no unified opposition presidential arrangement has emerged between them. The implications extend particularly to the North-West, where Kwankwaso retains established political networks, and to constituencies where Obi’s 2023 presidential support remains relevant historical evidence. But there is no fresh polling establishing how voters would respond to either cooperation or continued competition. Presidential assessment: Separate ADC and NDC candidatures reaffirmed; no measurable change in voter preferences. THE ELECTORAL MAP : TODAY’S ADJUSTMENTS State/region Development Assessment Kaduna: Former El-Rufai allies move from ADC to APC. Organisational realignment confirmed Kogi APC wins all 260 local-government positions. Local-government control confirmed Kano/North-West: Kwankwaso rejects withdrawal from presidential race; separate NDC campaign reaffirmed Osun/Anambra/Rivers: Existing cross-party presidential arrangements; no additional adjustment Gombe/Ogun Governorship nomination disputes There is no newly verified INEC-conducted election result or credible voter-preference poll requiring a further national assessment. No fresh development establishes a measurable change in support for the PDP, Labour Party, NNPP or significant regional parties. THE BOTTOM LINE This weekend offers three different measures of political strength. Kaduna demonstrates how defections can reshape party organisations. Kogi provides evidence of control over elected local-government offices. And the dispute between the ADC and NDC illustrates the difficulties of coordinating separate presidential ambitions. But none should be mistaken for a reliable prediction of the 2027 election. The important distinction remains between political organisation, electoral participation and actual voter preference. The immediate developments to watch are whether Kaduna’s defections produce verifiable changes in party structures, whether detailed Kogi election data become available, and whether the ADC-NDC disagreement develops into a substantive change in their coalition positions. item.title: Bomb threat forces flight to make emergency landing in Bulgaria
item.description: A bomb threat against an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna on Sunday forced the plane to divert to Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian authorities and the airline. The Austrian Airlines crew decided to make an emergency landing in Sofia after reportedly receiving a bomb threat as they neared Romania, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement, adding that the passengers were evacuated from the aircraft after landing. The Bulgarian air force scrambled a MiG-29 fighter jet to escort the airliner as part of established procedures, the transport ministry said. The airline told AFP that 51 passengers and six crew were aboard the flight, and that a security search of the aircraft — an Airbus A320 — was launched after it safely landed in Sofia about a half hour after the threat. “Once the search of the aircraft is complete, the passengers will be rebooked onto alternative flights as quickly as possible,” the airline said. According to Flightradar24 data, the aircraft, registered OE-LZE, entered Romanian airspace at around 9:10pm before turning south and heading back towards Bulgaria, where it landed in Sofia. Data from another flight-tracking platform, ADS-B Exchange, indicates that the aircraft was transmitting squawk code 7700 — a signal for a general emergency — at around the same time. The transport ministry said that a crisis response team has been set up and the relevant authorities have launched an investigation into the incident. In a separate incident late last month, the co-pilot aboard a flybubai airline flight headed to Tel Aviv from Dubai attacked the captain and allegedly planned to intentionally crash the plane but was stopped by the captain, passengers and crew. Last week, Croatia and Germany both scrambled fighter jets after a commercial flight from the Greek holiday island of Corfu to the German city of Nuremberg accidentally sent out a hijacking alert. item.title: Ibori hails Dele Cole’s role in resource control struggle
item.description: By Dapo Akinrefon Former Delta State Governor, Chief James Ibori, has mourned prominent Niger Delta leader Patrick Dele Cole, praising his commitment to the struggle for true federalism and resource control. Cole, who was born on August 4, 1940, in Abonnema, in the Kalabari Kingdom of present-day Rivers State, died in London at the age of 86. In a statement titled “PDC: So Long My Leader,” Ibori described the late Cole as a steadfast advocate of the Niger Delta cause who remained loyal to his roots despite the political implications of his position. He said Cole played a significant role in the region’s struggle for true federalism and resource control, adding that his commitment to the aspirations of the Niger Delta people remained firm even while he served as a special adviser in the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo. According to Ibori, Cole’s dedication to the region demonstrated his willingness to stand with his people at a time when doing so could carry considerable political costs. He added that the late leader’s political choices were guided by his commitment to the interests and legitimate aspirations of the Niger Delta people. “He was a prominent leader in the Niger Delta who stood firmly with us in our struggle for true federalism and resource control. Even while serving as a special adviser in President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, he remained committed to his people and their legitimate aspirations,” Ibori said. He added that Cole’s actions reflected deep loyalty to his roots and an unwavering commitment to the Niger Delta cause. “At a time when such a stance could carry significant political costs, he chose to stand with his people,” he said. Ibori urged the family of the late statesman to take solace in God, saying Cole’s contributions to Nigeria’s development, particularly in the Niger Delta, would remain cherished. item.title: Police arrest 56-year-old man over wife’s death in Ogun
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 56-year-old man, Madarikan Emehinola, in connection with a suspected arson incident that claimed the life of his 40-year-old wife, Igbagbo Erobe, in the Igbo-Edu area of Ogun Waterside Local Government Area. The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi. According to the statement, the incident was reported at the Abigi Divisional Police Headquarters after information was received that a house had been set ablaze, resulting in the woman’s death. “The Ogun State Police Command has a 56-year-old man, Madarikan Emehinola, in custody in connection with a suspected arson incident that claimed the life of his 40-year-old wife, Igbagbo Erobe,” the statement said. The police said the deceased’s body had been deposited at a mortuary for a post-mortem examination to establish the circumstances surrounding her death. The command added that arrangements were being made to transfer the case to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Eleweran, Abeokuta, for further investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Ogun State, Bode Ojajuni, assured the public that the case would be investigated thoroughly and professionally in accordance with the law. Ojajuni also reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that allegations involving serious crimes received appropriate investigative attention. The police urged members of the public to report suspicious activities promptly and provide credible information that could assist crime prevention and ongoing investigations. The circumstances surrounding the fire and the woman’s death remain under investigation. The suspect’s arrest does not establish guilt. item.title: ‘It felt like a fresh start’ — Carrick reacts to Man United’s draw at Leeds
item.description: Michael Carrick said Manchester United’s hard-fought 1-1 draw at bitter rivals Leeds on Sunday felt like a “fresh start” even though their long wait for a win goes on. Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo’s first-half opener at Elland Road, extending United’s winless run to six matches in all competitions. But Carrick saw positive signs five days after the 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid, which sparked Lisandro Martinez’s criticism of the club hierarchy over a lack of summer investment. “We’re not getting too carried away because we haven’t won the game,” said the Red Devils boss, who started the Argentina defender at Leeds but had to replace him at the break due to a thigh problem. “I think if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons then you get what you deserve in the end. “It felt like a bit of a fresh start, if I’m honest, today in where we’re at and accepting it and doing something about it. “It definitely shows that the boys are desperate to do well for each other as much as anything else and how much they appreciate playing for this football club, because there was a real purpose to the group over the last couple of days.” United head to Como on Wednesday looking for a first victory since last month’s Champions League opener against Sabah before attempting to kickstart their Premier League campaign at home to Bournemouth. item.description: By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has criticised the Minister of State for Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, over comments on President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects, urging the Federal Government to prioritise economic relief for Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement on Sunday, the association’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, said the government should focus on addressing rising living costs, high petrol prices, declining purchasing power and widespread economic hardship rather than discussing the President’s chances of securing a second term. HURIWA faulted what it described as Oyedele’s preoccupation with Tinubu’s electoral prospects, arguing that Nigerians needed concrete explanations of how the administration intended to ease financial pressures on households and stimulate economic activity. The association also questioned suggestions that international investors and financial markets were anticipating Tinubu’s victory in 2027, maintaining that the election outcome would ultimately be determined by Nigerian voters. item.title: Kebbi Govt disputes UNDP poverty rating, faults ADC
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Government has disputed a reported poverty rating attributed to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), describing it as outdated and accusing opposition politicians of using it to criticise the administration of Governor Nasir Idris. The state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed Birnin Kebbi, stated this on Sunday at a press conference held at the Government House in Birnin Kebbi. He claimed that the report being cited covered data from 2018, during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari, and alleged that former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, had brought it to public attention to discredit the Idris administration. The commissioner, however, did not provide details of the report or documentary evidence to substantiate his claims in the information made available. He urged opposition politicians, including those in the African Democratic Congress (ADC), to focus on proposals for the state’s development rather than what he described as efforts to discredit the government. Birnin Kebbi also appealed to residents not to be swayed by what he called politically motivated claims ahead of the forthcoming general elections. He said the Idris administration had made progress in addressing economic challenges and poverty in the state since assuming office three years ago. The commissioner attributed the economic difficulties inherited by the current administration to what he described as a period of economic dislocation and widespread poverty, but did not provide comparative data to support the government’s assessment. On insecurity, he said the state government had supported security operations through the provision of patrol vehicles and logistics, as well as the establishment of military bases in communities considered vulnerable to attacks by armed groups. He also accused Malami of failing to show sufficient concern for communities affected by insecurity during his time in public office, alleging that the former minister had not visited some affected towns to sympathise with victims. Birnin Kebbi further criticised Malami’s comments on insecurity, arguing that his record in public office should be considered when assessing his criticisms of the current administration. The commissioner also made allegations concerning Malami’s conduct while in office, but no supporting evidence was provided in the statement made available for this report. The claims against Malami and the opposition’s position on the poverty rating were not independently verified. The UNDP report cited by the state government’s critics was not provided for review, and the organisation’s position on the dispute was not available. item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A Catholic priest, Rev. Fr. item.title: Macron condemns “shocking” scenes of violence across France
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned on Sunday what he called the “dissenters” who looted ​and vandalised cities in “shocking” scenes across France ‌on the sidelines of protests over the cost of living. “Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: ​what was going through their minds? How ​can French people do this to France?”, Macron said in a televised address to the ​nation. “Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses ​it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame.” Macron, whose final six months in office are being shaped by ​mounting political, fiscal, and social pressures, said he ​had ordered a review to determine whether there had been ‌failings ⁠in intelligence gathering or police preparedness before protests that were later marred by looting and violence. He said prefects and mayors would be empowered ​to ban certain ​gatherings where ⁠necessary. Macron also said he had asked the government to bring together ​students, teachers, lawmakers, trade union representatives and ​business ⁠leaders this week to formulate what he described as “concrete proposals” to address the crisis, without providing ⁠further ​details. “We must sit around the ​table and build solutions together,” he said. item.title: Makinde warns successors against dismantling Oyo agencies
item.description: …Says rule of law, security bodies key to investment, growth By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has challenged his successors to sustain institutions established by his administration, warning that dismantling them could undermine efforts to strengthen governance, maintain public order and drive the state’s long-term development. Makinde spoke at the weekend during the commissioning of the new office complex of the Oyo State Rule of Law Enforcement Authority (OYRLEA), where he said the sustainability of the institutions would be a major test of his successors’ commitment to good governance. He maintained that the agencies established since he assumed office in 2019 were designed to serve the state beyond his tenure and should not be abolished without justification. Among the institutions he listed were OYRLEA; the Oyo State Security Network Agency, known as Amotekun; the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency (OYSADA); the Oyo State Project Performance Monitoring Agency; the Oyo State Mobilisation Agency for Socioeconomic Development (OYMASED); and the Oyo State Anti-Corruption Agency (OYACA). According to the governor, administrations genuinely committed to Oyo State’s progress should sustain the agencies rather than seek to dismantle them. “At the heart of good governance is the rule of law. When people know their rights and security agencies enforce the law without bias, you have order, investors come in, and the economy improves. That is what we have experienced in Oyo State,” Makinde said. He said his administration’s legacy should be measured not only by infrastructure projects but also by the institutions established to promote continuity, stability and accountability in governance. Makinde added that he expected the agencies to remain relevant after his tenure, describing their establishment as part of a deliberate effort to build structures capable of supporting the state’s development over the long term. The governor also commended OYRLEA Chairperson, Justice Aderonke Aderemi (retd.), for her commitment to the Authority’s mandate, saying he had no regrets appointing her despite disagreements they had encountered at certain points. The event featured the commissioning of the Authority’s new office complex and the unveiling of its maiden magazine, which its leadership described as significant milestones in its operations. In his goodwill message, Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Adebo Ogundoyin, said the legislation establishing OYRLEA reflected the Assembly’s determination to provide legal frameworks for addressing practical challenges confronting the state. Ogundoyin said the Authority was responsible for enforcing laws relating to environmental protection, sanitation, waste control, road traffic management, open rearing and grazing, among other matters. He described the responsibilities as important to public order and development, urging the Authority to discharge its duties transparently and responsibly.

item.title: Man, son burnt to death in Jos tricycle crash
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — A man and his son were reportedly burnt to death after a commercial tricycle, popularly known as Keke NAPEP, caught fire following a road crash in the Sabon Barki area of Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State on Sunday. Three other persons sustained injuries in the incident, which occurred at about 4:20 p.m. as the family was reportedly returning from church. An eyewitness, Kefas Gyang, said the tricycle was allegedly hit by a bus, resulting in the crash and subsequent fire. Gyang said the man’s wife sustained a broken leg, while two other children and the tricycle operator were taken to hospital for treatment. Recounting the incident, the eyewitness said he was returning from work when he noticed people crying and moved closer to ascertain what had happened. “I was passing by on my way from work when I saw people crying and I went closer to find out what had happened and saw people trying to rescue the victims,” he said. “But the fire was too much for us to handle. It was beyond our strength, and we could not do much to rescue them from the burning tricycle.” Gyang said the man and his son were burnt beyond recognition in the fire, adding that he did not witness the actual collision. “When the other vehicle hit the Keke, I was not there. I only came across the scene afterwards and saw people crying,” he said. He further alleged that the driver of the other vehicle fled the scene after the crash. Efforts to reach the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) for comments on the incident were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: VIDEO: Wike Leads Assembly Members, Council Chairmen, Others To Meet With Fubara
item.description: Barely two weeks after an earlier meeting between political leaders loyal to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, both camps have held another round of talks aimed at consolidating ongoing reconciliation efforts in the state. Wike led a delegation comprising mainly members of the Rivers State House of Assembly, including its Speaker, Martin Amaewhule, and the 23 local government council chairmen, to meet with Governor Fubara and his supporters at the governor’s private residence in Port Harcourt. Also part of the delegation was the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Rivers State, Kingsley Chinda. The latest meeting represents another attempt by the political leaders to build on previous engagements and strengthen efforts to resolve the protracted political crisis that has polarised Rivers State and strained relations between Governor Fubara and members of the State House of Assembly. However, the extent to which the latest meeting will translate into a lasting resolution remains to be seen, amid concerns over the perceived dominance of Wike’s camp in the leadership of the local government councils and the selection of candidates for the 2027 elections, with members of Fubara’s camp seemingly left out of the political arrangements. ﻿ The post VIDEO: Wike Leads Assembly Members, Council Chairmen, Others To Meet With Fubara appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Madueke’s Late Strike Helps Arsenal Snatch Victory Over Nottingham Forest
item.description: Arsenal struck late to beat Nottingham Forest and keep the pressure on Premier League leaders Manchester City on Sunday, while struggling Manchester United dropped more points in a draw at Leeds. The Gunners faced Forest a day after pacesetters City celebrated a seventh win in seven games at home to Ipswich — shrugging off the fallout from the club’s guilty verdict for serious financial irregularities. Defending champions Arsenal huffed and puffed against Oliver Glasner’s struggling side but finally secured the breakthrough when substitute Noni Madueke’s effort found the net in the 80th minute after a deflection off Jair Cunha. The goal was Arsenal’s only shot on target in a disjointed performance that lacked attacking quality, but they are showing an impressive ability to grind out results when not at their best. item.title: EPL: Leeds Frustrate Man United To Pile Pressure On Carrick
item.description: Manchester United ended a turbulent week with a frustrating 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday that does little to ease the pressure on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick. The Red Devils travelled to the home of their bitter rivals, desperate to find a spark after just two wins in nine games in all competitions this season. The sense of a growing crisis at the club was exacerbated in midweek by an outburst from defender Lisandro Martinez, who took aim at the United hierarchy after a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. The Argentina centre-back said Carrick, in his first full season in charge at Old Trafford, had been left with an under-strength squad after an underwhelming summer transfer window. The United boss insisted on Friday that United had “moved on” from the incident, and Martinez was named in the starting line-up at Elland Road. Both teams were fully committed in a feisty start to the match in Leeds but there was little goalmouth action. The first effort on target came in the 26th minute when United goalkeeper Senne Lammens clawed away a Nico Elvedi header destined for the top corner after bouncing up off the turf. Bryan Mbeumo, playing as United’s target man, headed wastefully wide a minute later after a fine cross from Youri Tielemans and then shot tamely at Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford. But he finally broke the deadlock in the 35th minute when Tielemans again delivered a low ball from the right which Mbeumo guided into the bottom corner for his fourth Premier League goal of the season. Martinez went off at half-time as Morocco’s Noussair Mazraoui was brought into the action. Leeds started strongly after the break and were level in the 51st minute when Dominic Calvert-Lewin controlled the ball on his chest and finished at full stretch after Tarik Muharemovic got his head to the ball following a corner. item.title: ‘France Is Burning,’ ‘Shattered’ By Immigration, Says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” France was reeling Sunday from widespread damage during protests the day before that, which left a historic town hall torched and led to 1,800 arrests, piling pressure on President Emmanuel Macron six months before elections to replace him. This photograph shows a portion of the partially burnt facade of the Limoges city hall a day after riot and looting following nationwide protests against the “high cost of living” in Limoges on October 18, 2026. PASCAL LACHENAUD / AFP Trump’s post follows similar comments from Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this, and they didn’t listen,” Vance wrote on X. “I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” he added. Vance, seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also linked it to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well.
